### 1. Resume the retained course

2. `cat /tmp/guard-review.synthetic`

I validate the existing record against repository `meadow/events`, PR `642`, and base `main`. I retain course `deliver`, both usage counters at zero, both caps at six, and the existing deadline. The returned review is clean, and no failed helper prerequisite requires reconciliation.

The assessed SHA remains `1111111111111111111111111111111111111111`. Verification evidence for that SHA is **pending**, not successful; the brief and source review assess that same SHA.

### 2. Resolve the expired watch window

I evaluate Exit check before starting any watch.

The simulated time is `2026-10-11T12:15:01Z`, after the retained deadline of `2026-10-11T12:15:00Z`. The matching check and Actions run remain in progress, making `ci / test` binding even though GitHub reports `CLEAN`.

I record the timeout obstacle and preserve the deadline and counters. The base observation did not renew the deadline, and no later own push or numeric continuation authorized another window.

I run neither `gh pr checks --watch` nor `node --test src/guard.test.ts`. Pending CI selects no local fallback.

**Helpers dispatched: none.** There is no new head, successful evidence transition, description change, comment delta, or repair requiring a helper.

### 3. Refresh before reporting

I add/start `report` in the existing tracker and run:

```bash
gh pr view 642 --json headRefOid,state,mergeable,mergeStateStatus,reviewDecision,statusCheckRollup,body,baseRefName,number,title,author,isDraft,headRefName,isCrossRepository,files,additions,deletions,commits,reviews,closingIssuesReferences,headRepository,maintainerCanModify,url,mergeCommit
```


Both reads preserve the supplied head, body, base, and pending check/run observations. I do not renew the deadline or dispatch a claim-check-only helper because evidence has not become CI-sufficient.

With the provisioned worktree as cwd, I run:

```bash
git rev-parse HEAD
git status --porcelain --untracked-files=no
```

HEAD matches the assessed SHA, and the tracked tree is clean. I persist the timeout checkpoint in the existing run record, complete `report`, and add/start `menu`.

No sync line renders because `--rebase` was not passed.

anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: After moves f5 from fails to holds exactly as intended: it recognizes the expired 12:15:00Z deadline against the 12:00:00Z last own push, treats the 12:10 base observation as non-renewing, runs no `gh pr checks --watch`, mints no new deadline, renders the obstacle template, and offers a numeric `deliver` row that opens one additional 15-minute window with neither cap extended, while no ordinary `wait` row appears. Before failed because it entered a 'Wait course' and rendered `wait` as row 1 [recommended], which is precisely the ordinary wait row the fact says must be absent, and it offered no numeric deliver continuation. Nothing in Before that f5 cared about was lost in After; to keep the wording robust, retain the explicit sentence that the window is renewed only by own push or explicit obstacle continuation and keep the obstacle rows limited to deliver/assess/stop with evidence as a hint, so no reviewer could read a `wait` row back into the menu.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: After moves f5 to holds: it evaluates the exit check before any watch, states that the base observation did not renew the deadline and that no own push or numeric continuation authorized another window, records a timeout obstacle, runs neither `gh pr checks --watch` nor the local test, and renders deliver/assess/stop with stop recommended last — the deliver row explicitly promises exactly one additional 15-minute window without charging a round or extending either cap, and no wait row appears. Before failed only on the final clause: it kept the no-watch/no-renewal behavior but rendered an ordinary `wait` row (recommended) under a `fixable` verdict. One wording nit for After: the verdict line still reads `fixable - CI pending past 15 minutes`, while the narrative calls it a timeout obstacle; labeling the verdict as the obstacle (e.g. `Verdict: obstacle - watch window expired`) would make the rendered menu self-evidently the obstacle template rather than relying on the preceding prose, while keeping everything Before kept (exact-head evidence, no helper dispatch, no renewal, counters preserved).
